The exemplar presents a level-4 reading of PBO, so the overstatement is what students will copy. (Lesson 8's Lab 4 interpretation and quiz explanation use the same phrasing; that is the L07-L08 slice's page.)

rows.evidence: Rule described correctly against the twin: long/short each currency by the sign of its 1-month log change (rates are USD per unit, so a rise is an appreciation), three overlapping monthly cohorts averaged (H3), equal weights; best by full-sample Sharpe of the 5 x 4 x 2 = 40 grid; 'fixed before the first run' is stated by Lesson 8 Lab 4's hypothesis ('The design was fixed before the code was first run'); all on the same 308 months 2001-02..2026-09; five uncounted choices; equicorrelation-matched N_eff and participation ratio as computed by Lab 4 (my recomputation: mean off-diagonal correlation 0.56659, participation ratio 2.37137, matched N_eff 7.7407 by brentq on (1-g)Phi^-1(1-1/n)+g Phi^-1(1-1/(ne)) = sqrt(1-rho) x bracket(40)); the Lesson 7 Section 4 / Proposition 4.2 statements match L07 (Proposition 4.2: the cross-sectional variance already prices correlation; an effective N belongs with the single-trial variance 1/T).

Every statement checked: hurdle = expected best of 40 skill-free rules with the trials' cross-sectional sd (L07 Def. 3.1 eq. 3); SR 0.0408 < SR0 0.0424; skewness/kurtosis enter the SE (L07 Thm 1.2); DSR = Phi((SR - SR0)/se) = 0.48898 = 1 - 0.51102, a one-sided p-value against the hurdle, explicitly not a probability of skill (L07 Remark 2.4); PSR 0.76951 = 1 - 0.23049; pairing N_eff 7.7407 with variance 1/308 gives SR0 0.082132 and DSR 0.22791 (my computation), 'far below our bar of 0.95' in both pairings.

Null H0: mean spot return <= 0 = contract integrity_report. StepM 0 of 40 at alpha 0.05 with 1,000 draws, block 10, seed 0, and 0 at blocks 5 and 20: reference romano_wolf and my independent StepM (scripts/stepm_indep.py: own loop-based stationary bootstrap, own step-down) both give 0 at 5, 10, 20; the observed max t is 0.717 against first critical values 2.48-2.59. BH 0 of 40 at q 0.05 (my BH on p = 1 - Phi(t)); smallest p 0.23682 belongs to column 2 = the selected rule; 0 p-values <= 0.05. FWER vs FDR correctly attributed; 'Failing to reject is not proof that the rules have no edge' is the correct reading. (For C4 level 4 the missing statement would be: a rule needed t > 2.57, i.e. a monthly Sharpe ratio above 2.573/sqrt(308) = 0.147, about 0.51 a year, to clear StepM's first critical value.)

Matches Lesson 5 Section 8 eq. (4): a long position earns r_t + (i* - i) + i* r_t; H.10 holds no interest rates; carry can raise or lower a rule's mean depending on whether it is long the high-yielders, so it can reorder the 40 rules; costs lower every rule; mean 0.55% a year (12 x monthly mean 0.000461) on volatility 3.91% (sqrt(12) x monthly sd); the tool assumptions named (approximate normality of the SR estimator vs kurtosis 15.2; comparable blocks; stationarity for the bootstrap) are the ones L08's comparison table lists. The cross term of (4) is omitted from the prose, harmlessly.

Three items, each fixed in advance with a result: carry-inclusive rerun with the bar (see memo-exemplar-b-c1-threshold for its PBO wording); a holdout 1971-01..1998-12 on the 9 currencies with a rate there (verified: AUD, CAD, CHF, DKK, GBP, JPY, NOK, NZD, SEK complete for all 336 months; EUR starts 1999-01; the review used only prices from 1999-01) with a one-sided 5% t-test; costs from turnover. 'None of the three can make the rule fundable by itself' is consistent with the rule.

mutants.description: m01_bh_step_down.py: Benjamini-Hochberg run step-down: stops at the first ordered p-value above its line instead of taking the largest passing k.
m02_bh_sorted_mask.py: Benjamini-Hochberg returns the rejection mask in sorted (rank) order instead of the input order.
m03_bh_strict_inequality.py: Benjamini-Hochberg uses a strict inequality p_(k) < kq/m, so a p-value exactly on its line is not rejected.
m04_kurtosis_excess.py: sample_kurtosis returns excess kurtosis m4/m2**2 - 3 (the scipy default) where the contract requires raw kurtosis.
m05_se_divides_by_n.py: Sharpe-ratio standard error divides the variance bracket by n instead of n - 1.
m06_se_kurtosis_minus_three.py: Sharpe-ratio standard error uses (kurtosis - 3)/4 in the bracket, mixing the excess-kurtosis form with raw kurtosis.
m07_dsr_population_variance.py: Deflated Sharpe ratio takes the population variance (ddof=0) of the trial Sharpe ratios instead of ddof=1.
m08_ems_one_trial_returns_zero.py: expected_max_sharpe at N = 1 returns 0.0 instead of sr_mean (forgets the shift when there is no selection).
m09_sb_no_wraparound.py: Stationary bootstrap never wraps around: a block that would run past the last period starts a new block instead of continuing at index 0.
m10_sb_geometric_parameter_inverted.py: Stationary bootstrap uses mean_block as the restart probability (1/p in place of p), so every step starts a new block.
m11_rw_resamples_columns_independently.py: Romano-Wolf resamples each strategy with its own bootstrap index vector, breaking the cross-sectional dependence.
m12_rw_not_studentized.py: Romano-Wolf is not studentized: it compares raw mean differentials with centred bootstrap means instead of t-statistics.
m13_stepdown_weak_inequality.py: Step-down rejects hypotheses with t_obs >= c instead of t_obs > c.
m14_stepdown_interpolated_quantile.py: Step-down critical value is np.quantile(maxima, 1 - alpha) with linear interpolation instead of the ceil((1-alpha)B)-th order statistic.
m15_stepdown_floor_rank.py: Step-down critical value uses the floor((1-alpha)B)-th order statistic instead of the ceil((1-alpha)B)-th.
m16_stepdown_single_step.py: Step-down never recomputes the critical value: one max-T critical value over all hypotheses (single-step test).
m17_pbo_strict_logit.py: PBO counts logits < 0 instead of logits <= 0, so a median out-of-sample rank is not counted as overfit.
m18_pbo_drops_newest_rows.py: CSCV drops the newest T mod S rows instead of the oldest.
m19_pbo_ignores_ties_in_rank.py: CSCV out-of-sample rank ignores ties (1 + #lower, a 'min' rank) instead of the average rank with +0.5 per tie.
m20_report_two_sided_pvalues.py: integrity_report feeds Benjamini-Hochberg two-sided p-values 2(1 - Phi(|t|)) instead of one-sided p-values for H0: mean <= 0.
m21_report_no_block_reduction.py: integrity_report passes n_blocks to CSCV unchanged instead of reducing it to the largest even number <= min(n_blocks, T).
n01_imports_scipy_for_the_normal_cdf.py: Uses scipy.stats.norm for the PSR's normal CDF, a dependency the A8 contract forbids (NumPy and the standard library only).
n02_pbo_accepts_one_period_halves.py: CSCV omits the half-sample rule: with (T - T mod S) / 2 < 2 it runs on one-period half-samples instead of raising ValueError.
n03_rw_tiny_constant_for_constant_resample.py: Romano-Wolf studentizes a constant resampled column by np.finfo(float).tiny instead of the column's sample standard deviation.
n04_rw_skips_constant_draws.py: Romano-Wolf discards every bootstrap draw in which a resampled column is constant, instead of studentizing it by the column's sample standard deviation.
n05_report_silent_nan_pbo_on_short_samples.py: integrity_report runs on fewer than 4 periods and reports pbo = nan instead of raising ValueError.
n06_sharpe_flattens_two_dimensional_input.py: Series validation flattens a two-dimensional input with ravel() instead of raising ValueError.
n07_rw_bootstrap_uses_full_sample_sd.py: Romano-Wolf studentizes every bootstrap draw by the full-sample standard deviation instead of the draw's own std(d*_k, ddof=1).
n08_rw_bootstrap_sd_default_ddof.py: Romano-Wolf computes the bootstrap draws' standard deviations with np.std's default ddof=0, while the observed statistics use ddof=1.

n09_pbo_metric_plain_ratio.py: CSCV's subsample Sharpe metric is plain mean / std, ignoring the contract's rule for a constant subsample (0.0 if its mean is 0, +-inf by the sign of the mean otherwise).
n10_sb_first_block_starts_at_zero.py: Stationary bootstrap starts the first block at index 0 instead of at a uniform random index.
n11_moments_skip_series_validation.py: sample_skewness and sample_kurtosis skip the series validation, so a two-dimensional or non-finite input returns a number instead of raising ValueError.

p01_sharpe_zero_variance_by_std_equality.py: sharpe_ratio detects zero variance with std(x, ddof=1) == 0 instead of all values equal, so a constant non-dyadic series returns a huge Sharpe ratio instead of raising ValueError.

p02_rw_accepts_a_constant_column.py: romano_wolf omits the constant-column check, so a column with all values equal is studentized by its (zero or tiny) standard deviation instead of raising ValueError.

p03_rw_constant_resample_by_std_equality.py: romano_wolf detects a constant resampled column with std(d*_k, ddof=1) == 0 instead of all values equal, so a constant non-dyadic resample is divided by a tiny floating-point standard deviation.

p04_cscv_constant_subsample_by_std_equality.py: CSCV's subsample metric detects a constant subsample with std == 0 instead of all values equal, so a constant non-dyadic subsample gets a huge finite Sharpe ratio instead of +-inf.
p05_cscv_floors_the_subsample_sd.py: CSCV floors the subsample standard deviation at 1e-12 to avoid dividing by zero, so a constant non-zero subsample gets a large finite metric instead of +-inf.

p06_moments_zero_variance_by_m2_equality.py: sample_skewness and sample_kurtosis detect zero variance with m2 == 0 instead of all values equal, so a constant non-dyadic series returns a meaningless number instead of raising ValueError.
p07_sb_accepts_mean_block_below_one.py: stationary_bootstrap_indices does not validate mean_block, so mean_block < 1 (a restart probability above one) returns indices instead of raising ValueError.

q01_moments_not_rescaled.py: sample_skewness and sample_kurtosis compute their moments on the raw series (only the Sharpe ratio is rescaled), so a fourth power overflows at 1e155 and a square underflows at 2**-1000.

q02_rw_one_scale_for_the_whole_matrix.py: romano_wolf rescales the whole differentials matrix by the one power of two of its largest absolute value instead of each column by its own, so a column far smaller than the largest underflows when squared.

q03_rw_reseeds_inside_the_loop.py: romano_wolf creates rng = np.random.default_rng(seed) inside the bootstrap loop, so every draw reuses the same index vector instead of drawing n_boot vectors in order from one generator.

q04_rw_vectorized_index_draws.py: romano_wolf draws all n_boot index vectors at once from one generator (vectorized) instead of calling stationary_bootstrap_indices(T, mean_block, rng) once per draw in order, as the contract now requires.
q05_cscv_constant_subsample_scores_zero.py: CSCV scores every constant subsample 0.0 (zero variance read as zero Sharpe ratio) instead of +-inf by the sign of its value.

q06_rw_constant_column_by_std_equality.py: romano_wolf detects a constant column of differentials with std(d_k, ddof=1) == 0 instead of all values equal, so a constant non-dyadic column is studentized by a tiny standard deviation instead of raising ValueError.
q07_sb_mean_block_nan_accepted.py: stationary_bootstrap_indices checks only mean_block < 1, so a NaN mean_block (every comparison False) passes and yields one block instead of raising ValueError.

q08_se_overflow_escapes.py: sharpe_ratio_std squares the Sharpe ratio with sharpe**2, so a huge Sharpe ratio raises OverflowError instead of the contract's ValueError for a variance bracket that overflows.
q09_rw_alpha_unchecked.py: romano_wolf does not validate alpha (it calls the step-down loop directly), so alpha outside (0, 1) returns decisions instead of raising ValueError.

q10_dsr_trial_variance_not_rescaled.py: deflated_sharpe_ratio takes np.var(trial_sharpes, ddof=1) on the raw values, so a variance beyond the largest float warns and returns instead of raising ValueError.

q11_rw_resample_in_column_scale.py: romano_wolf studentizes each resample in its column's scale (rescales the column once, not the resample), so a resample of values far smaller than its column's largest has a square that underflows and a zero standard deviation.

q12_cscv_subsample_in_column_scale.py: CSCV computes each subsample's Sharpe ratio in its configuration's full-sample scale (rescales each column once, not each subsample), so a subsample of values far smaller than the column's largest has a zero standard deviation.
q13_bh_accepts_nan_pvalues.py: benjamini_hochberg checks the p-value range with comparisons only, so a NaN p-value (every comparison False) passes and is never rejected instead of raising ValueError.
q14_psr_benchmark_nan_only.py: probabilistic_sharpe_ratio rejects only a NaN benchmark (math.isnan), so an infinite sr_benchmark returns 0.0 or 1.0 instead of raising ValueError.

r01_scale_by_largest_value_not_magnitude.py: The power-of-two rescaling takes its exponent from the largest value (x.max()) instead of the largest absolute value, so a series dominated by a large negative return overflows when it is 'rescaled'.

r02_rw_one_seed_per_draw.py: romano_wolf seeds a fresh generator for every bootstrap draw (np.random.default_rng([seed, b])) instead of drawing all n_boot index vectors in order from the single rng = np.random.default_rng(seed).

r03_cscv_constant_subsample_ignores_sign.py: CSCV scores every constant nonzero subsample +inf, ignoring its sign, so a configuration that loses the same amount every period looks like the best in-sample.
r04_rw_constant_resample_population_sd.py: romano_wolf studentizes a constant resampled column by the column's population standard deviation (np.std default ddof=0) instead of std(d_k, ddof=1).
r05_integer_check_by_int_cast.py: Integer arguments are checked with int(x) != x, so an infinite n_obs, n_trials, n_boot or n_blocks raises OverflowError instead of ValueError.
r06_ems_textbook_quantile.py: expected_max_sharpe evaluates the textbook Phi^-1(1 - 1/N), which is infinite once 1 - 1/N rounds to 1 (N beyond 2**53), instead of -Phi^-1(1/N).

r07_se_keeps_numpy_scalars.py: sharpe_ratio_std does arithmetic on its scalar arguments as given, so a NumPy float64 Sharpe ratio whose square overflows raises a RuntimeWarning instead of the contract's ValueError.
r08_trialset_truncates_selected.py: TrialSet casts selected and periods_per_year with int() before validating them, so a fractional selected silently picks the column below it.

r09_rw_centre_overflow_unguarded.py: romano_wolf re-expresses the column mean in the resample's scale without guarding the overflow, so a column spanning more than 2**1024 between its largest value and a resample's largest value warns instead of giving the contract's -inf statistic.

r10_integer_check_rejects_numpy_integers.py: Integer arguments are checked with isinstance(x, int), so a NumPy integer (np.int64 from np.argmax or an array element) is rejected with ValueError although the contract accepts NumPy numbers.

r11_psr_keeps_numpy_benchmark.py: probabilistic_sharpe_ratio subtracts a NumPy-scalar benchmark without converting it with float(), so an extreme np.float64 benchmark raises an overflow RuntimeWarning.

r12_se_n_obs_finite_not_integral.py: sharpe_ratio_std checks only that n_obs is finite and at least 2, not that it is an integer, so a fractional n_obs such as 2.5 returns a standard error instead of raising ValueError.

r13_trialset_periods_per_year_finite_not_integral.py: TrialSet checks only that periods_per_year is finite and at least 1, not that it is an integer, so 251.5 is silently truncated to 251 instead of raising ValueError.

s01_rw_float_seed_not_converted.py: romano_wolf validates seed as an integer but passes it to np.random.default_rng unconverted, so an integral float seed such as 7.0, which the contract accepts, raises TypeError.

s02_pbo_float_n_blocks_not_converted.py: probability_of_backtest_overfitting validates n_blocks as an integer but uses it unconverted, so an integral float n_blocks such as 8.0, which the contract accepts, raises TypeError (slice indices must be integers).
s03_integer_bound_inclusive.py: Integer arguments are bounded by magnitude at most 2**1000 instead of below 2**1000, so n_trials or n_obs equal to 2**1000 is accepted instead of raising ValueError.

s04_integer_bound_for_ints_only.py: The 2**1000 bound on integer arguments is applied to Python and NumPy integers only, so an integral float such as 1e305 is accepted as n_trials or n_obs instead of raising ValueError.

s05_zero_variance_by_ptp.py: Zero variance is tested with np.ptp(x) == 0, whose subtraction overflows with a RuntimeWarning for a series spanning more than the largest float, such as [1e308, -1e308, 5e307].

s06_scale_divides_by_power_of_two.py: The power-of-two rescaling divides by 2.0**e instead of calling np.ldexp, so a series whose largest absolute value is at least 2**1023 (about 9e307) overflows the divisor to inf with a RuntimeWarning.

s07_rw_studentization_unguarded.py: romano_wolf guards the overflow of the re-expressed column mean but not of the studentized difference, so a resample far smaller than its column warns (overflow in divide) instead of giving the contract's quiet +-inf statistic.

s08_report_pvalues_not_rescaled.py: integrity_report computes the trials' t-statistics for the BH p-values on the unscaled returns, so a trial set of tiny or huge returns (2**-600 or 2**600 times ordinary ones) underflows or overflows its variances and warns.
s09_report_romano_wolf_ignores_seed.py: integrity_report does not forward its seed, so its Romano-Wolf bootstrap is always drawn from np.random.default_rng(0) whatever seed the caller passes.
s10_report_romano_wolf_ignores_alpha.py: integrity_report does not forward alpha, so its Romano-Wolf rejections always use romano_wolf's default level 0.05 whatever alpha the caller passes.

s11_dsr_rejects_equal_trial_sharpes.py: deflated_sharpe_ratio applies the zero-variance rule of a return series to trial_sharpes, so equal trial Sharpe ratios (variance 0, so SR0 = 0) raise ValueError instead of giving the PSR against 0.
t01_report_bh_uses_alpha_not_q.py: integrity_report validates q but runs Benjamini-Hochberg at alpha, the StepM level, so bh_rejections ignore the caller's q.

t02_report_romano_wolf_ignores_mean_block.py: integrity_report does not forward mean_block, so its Romano-Wolf bootstrap always uses romano_wolf's default mean block length 10 whatever the caller passes.
t03_report_pvalues_population_sd.py: integrity_report computes the trials' t-statistics for the BH p-values with np.std's default ddof=0 instead of std(ddof=1).

t04_stepm_per_hypothesis_critical_values.py: Step-down uses each hypothesis's own bootstrap quantile (the ceil((1-alpha)B)-th smallest t*_bk of column k) instead of the quantile of the maximum over the active set, so it controls no family-wise error.
t05_cscv_interleaved_blocks.py: CSCV forms its S blocks by interleaving rows (block i holds rows i, i+S, i+2S, ...) instead of consecutive runs of periods.
t06_report_annualizes_by_periods.py: integrity_report annualizes the selected Sharpe ratio by multiplying by periods_per_year instead of its square root.
t07_sb_start_index_off_by_one.py: Stationary bootstrap draws block starts with rng.integers(0, n - 1), an exclusive upper bound one too low, so the last period never starts a block.
t08_ems_hard_coded_forty_trial_bracket.py: expected_max_sharpe hard-codes Lesson 7 Example 3.2's bracket 2.1895 for N = 40 trials instead of evaluating the formula at the given N.
t09_dsr_ignores_n_trials.py: deflated_sharpe_ratio ignores an explicit n_trials and always deflates by len(trial_sharpes).
t10_psr_sign_reversed.py: probabilistic_sharpe_ratio subtracts in the wrong order, Phi((SR* - SR)/se), so it returns one minus the PSR.
